scenarios.title: The Club Signs {J}'s Replacement
scenarios.text: The club announces a new signing: twenty-one, quick, plays {J}'s position, five-year contract. At the press conference the sporting director uses the phrase “succession planning”.

choices.label: Mentor the new kid
choices.text: {J} takes {K} under his wing. The kid calls him “old man” with real affection. {M} watches it with respect.

choices.label: Fight for your shirt
choices.text: {J} trains like he's nineteen again. For now, the shirt stays his.

choices.label: Ask about your future
choices.text: {M} is honest: “You'll play less. But I want you here.” It's both a comfort and a sentence.

scenarios.title: {M} Suggests {J} Plays Deeper
scenarios.text: {M} watches the GPS data and makes a suggestion: “Your legs aren't what they were. Your brain is better than ever. Play deeper. Let the game come to you.”

choices.label: Embrace the new role
choices.text: Playing deeper, {J} sees the whole pitch for the first time. His passing becomes the best in the squad.

choices.label: Stay where you are
choices.text: {J} stays wide. For a few months it works. Then a twenty-year-old full-back leaves him for dead.

scenarios.title: Maybe the Last Contract
scenarios.text: Contract talks at thirty-two-plus are different. The club offers one year, less money, an option for a second year “based on appearances”. A club in a smaller league offers two years and more money. Retirement is also an option nobody says out loud.

choices.label: Stay at a club you love
choices.text: {J} signs the one-year deal. The fans chant his name at the next match.

choices.label: Follow the money
choices.desc: One more payday for the family.
choices.hint: Some fans will call it mercenary.
choices.text: {J} tells his agent to make the move happen. The smaller club will be in touch when the window opens.

scenarios.title: The Academy Wants {J} to Coach Part-Time
scenarios.text: The club's academy director asks if {J} would coach the U-16s twice a week, alongside playing. His coaching badges make it possible. The kids already know who he is.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.text: Twice a week, twenty teenagers hang on his every word. He discovers he loves it.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: {J} declines for now. The director says the door is open.

scenarios.title: A Testimonial Match for {J}
scenarios.text: The club announces a testimonial match in {J}'s honour: old teammates, former coaches, his children as mascots. The proceeds will go wherever he chooses.

choices.label: Your foundation or a children's charity
choices.text: Twenty thousand people come. Every ticket funds scholarships. Old teammates fly in from three continents.

choices.label: Your family
choices.text: The proceeds, {gift}, go to his parents. His father makes a speech at halftime and nobody can hear a word over the cheering.

scenarios.title: The Body Starts to Say No
scenarios.text: Three days to recover from a match instead of one. Knee strapping that takes twenty minutes. A sprint that used to feel like flying now feels like pushing a car. {J} hears the young players laughing about something and realises he doesn't understand the joke.
scenarios.prompt: How do you feel about it?

choices.label: Make peace with it
choices.text: {J} accepts it. Strangely, the matches feel more precious now.

choices.label: Fight it with everything
choices.text: Extra recovery, extra stretching, extra everything. He buys himself one more good season, maybe.

scenarios.title: Opposition Fans Applaud {J}
scenarios.text: At an away ground where he's been booed for fifteen years, the home fans stand and applaud when {J} is substituted. Word has spread that this may be his last season.

scenarios.title: {J} Takes a Teenager Under His Wing
scenarios.text: {K}, seventeen, reminds {J} of himself: talented, nervous, too much hair gel. The kid follows him around like a shadow and asks a hundred questions a day.
scenarios.prompt: What do you teach him first?

choices.label: Professionalism
choices.text: {J} teaches him the boring things nobody told {J} at that age. A year later, the kid is in the first team.

choices.label: How to handle money
choices.text: {J} tells him every financial mistake he ever made. The kid writes them all down.

choices.label: How to enjoy it
choices.text: “It goes faster than you think. Enjoy it.” The kid doesn't understand yet. He will.

scenarios.title: TV Wants {J} as a Pundit
scenarios.text: A television network invites {J} to guest on their weekend highlights show. If it goes well, a permanent job after retirement.

choices.label: Do it
choices.hint: Your colleagues will watch every word.

ok.text: {J} is a natural: sharp, funny, honest without being cruel. The producer calls the next day.

bad.text: {J} is stiff and nervous on camera. The clip of him freezing becomes a meme.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. Not yet.

scenarios.title: An Old Rival Retires
scenarios.text: {T}, the defender who kicked {J} in a hundred matches over fifteen years, announces his retirement. In the farewell interview, he says {J} was the toughest opponent he ever faced.

choices.label: Send a heartfelt message
choices.text: “You made me better. Thank you for every bruise.” The message goes viral.

choices.label: A joke
choices.text: The rival replies with a laughing emoji and a photo of their worst tackle. The internet adores it.

scenarios.title: From Star to Senior Voice
scenarios.text: {J} plays less now. But in the dressing room, his voice carries further than ever. Young players come to him with problems they won't take to the coaches.

scenarios.title: {P} Asks When It Will End
scenarios.text: {P} says it at the kitchen table one evening, gently: “The children want their father at home. When will you stop?”

choices.label: “At the end of this season”
choices.text: {P} holds his hand. The decision feels lighter once it's said out loud.

choices.label: “When my body tells me”
choices.text: {P} nods, unconvinced.

scenarios.title: {J} Breaks a Club Appearance Record
scenarios.text: With his 300th appearance, {J} becomes one of the most capped players in the history of everywhere he's played. Before kick-off, the club presents a framed shirt with the number 300.

scenarios.title: Hall of Fame Nomination
scenarios.text: The league announces its Hall of Fame nominees for the year. {J}'s name is on the list, alongside players he idolised as a child.

scenarios.title: Probably {J}'s Last Derby
scenarios.text: Everyone knows this is probably {J}'s last derby. The rival fans, who have abused him for fifteen years, have made a banner. Nobody knows yet what it says.
scenarios.prompt: Walk to the rival end before kick-off?

choices.label: Walk over and applaud them
choices.hint: Could be beautiful. Could be ugly.

out.text: The banner says: “THANK YOU FOR THE WAR.” Both ends applaud. Grown men cry.
The banner is an insult. A coin flies. He walks back smiling anyway.

choices.label: Stay focused
choices.text: {J} warms up like it's any other derby. Later, he notices the banner says thank you.

scenarios.title: {J} Writes His Retirement Letter
scenarios.text: He promised {P}. One night, at the kitchen table, {J} writes the letter he's been composing in his head for a year. He doesn't send it yet. He reads it to himself four times.

scenarios.title: Old Man Still Has It
scenarios.text: Twenty minutes off the bench in a match the team was losing, and {J} changes it: an assist, a goal-saving tackle, a leadership masterclass. The commentator says, “Experience. You can't buy it.”

scenarios.title: The Club Asks {J} to Take a Pay Cut
scenarios.text: Finances are tight. The sporting director asks the senior players to accept reduced wages for the rest of the season. {J} earns the most of anyone over thirty.

choices.label: Accept, and say so publicly
choices.text: {J} takes a 30% cut and says so in an interview. Within a week, every senior player has followed.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: {J} refuses politely. The board doesn't forget.

scenarios.title: First Club Wants {J} Back for a Final Chapter
scenarios.text: The club where it all started calls: would {J} come home for one last season? Less money, smaller league. The fans who saw him at sixteen are waiting.

choices.label: Tell your agent to make it happen
choices.text: The rumour leaks within an hour. The club's ticket office gets a thousand calls.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.desc: One more season at this level.
choices.text: {J} says not yet. The old club says the door will stay open.

scenarios.title: The Fear of One Bad Injury
scenarios.text: At thirty-two, every injury could be the last. {J} watches a teammate of the same age go down with a serious knee injury and is quiet for the rest of the day.

choices.label: Play more carefully
choices.text: {J} pulls out of a few 50-50s. Nobody notices except him.

choices.label: Play like always
choices.text: {J} keeps playing like he's twenty-five. His body hasn't sent the bill yet.

scenarios.title: Publisher Offers {J} an Autobiography Deal
scenarios.text: A publisher wants {J}'s autobiography: {fee} advance, a ghostwriter, a launch at the national book fair. It would mean telling the whole story, including the parts he's never told.

choices.label: Tell everything
choices.text: The book is brutally honest. It's a bestseller. Two former managers stop speaking to him.

choices.label: The nice version
choices.text: The book is warm and inspiring. Mostly read by kids. That's fine.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: {J} says the last chapter isn't written yet.

scenarios.title: Passing the Gloves
scenarios.text: The young goalkeeper who will replace {J} is talented and terrified. Every mistake in training, he looks at {J}. {J} recognises the look.

scenarios.title: A Teenager Runs Past {J}
scenarios.text: Sixty-fifth minute. A nineteen-year-old winger knocks the ball past {J} and simply outruns him. Ten years ago {J} would have caught him. Today he watches him go.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.text: After the match, {J} finds the kid and says, “You're going to be very good.” The kid will remember it forever.

choices.label: It hurts
choices.text: {J} drives home in silence. That night he watches old highlights of himself. He doesn't know whether it helps.

scenarios.title: Club Offers {J} an Ambassador Role After Retirement
scenarios.text: The club president offers {J} a job for life: club ambassador after retirement, representing the club around the world. A desk, a salary, a seat in the directors' box.

scenarios.title: Is This the Last Goal?
scenarios.text: {J} scores, and for a moment wonders: is this the last one? He celebrates a little longer than usual, arms wide, eyes on the crowd, trying to memorise it.

scenarios.title: The Physio's Honest Conversation
scenarios.text: The head physio, who has treated {J} for eight years, closes the treatment room door. “You can keep going. But every season now costs you something later. Your knees at sixty. Your back. I want you to know.”
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with that?

choices.label: Thank him and think about it
choices.text: {J} thanks him and starts thinking seriously about the end.

choices.label: Push on
choices.hint: Your later self will have opinions.
choices.text: {J} pushes on. One more season. Then one more.
